$meta.role: Design -> code map for @sayva/design-system. Every design token and contracted primitive is either implemented, or explicitly deferred/blocked with a reason. An entry with neither fails CI from Slice 3 onward.
$meta.scopeDecision: D1 - Phase 1 implements the token layer, the 10 Design System primitives and one shared overlay substrate hook. The 12 Design System patterns are out of scope; see outOfScope.patterns. The design's own phase1 flag marks 17 components, 7 of which are patterns this decision defers.

statusVocabulary.deferred: In Phase 1 scope, not yet implemented.
statusVocabulary.blocked: Cannot be implemented without a design decision. Carries a reason naming the open decision.
statusVocabulary.implemented: Present in code and covered by the parity test.
statusVocabulary.out-of-scope: Deliberately not in Phase 1. Carries a reason.

tokens.reason: Conflict C1 - Foundations SS15 states 28px, the Design System density prop states 26px. Both documents are canonical; the design owner must pick. Pending open decision D4. No Phase 1 component consumes it.

UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN - audit finding F9. The rule is stated in prose (2px accent ring, 2px offset, never removed) but no focus.ring.{color,width,offset} trio exists. Pending open decision D5. Must not be filled from convention (AC13).

components.note: Split across two slices: 14 (text, mono, number, textarea, select, date) and 15 (combobox, multi-facet).

Decision D3: the design contract lists the six domain lifecycle states as this component's states. @sayva/design-system must stay domain-free (ADR-002 DR-02/DR-03), so the implementation exposes the five presentational status token families as `tone` plus caller-supplied `glyph` and `label`. The lifecycle -> (glyph, tone) mapping is design data owned by apps/studio and parity-tested against this manifest in Slice 16.
Decision D3: states are reference-resolution states, not entity lifecycle states. `deprecated` is a presentational treatment the caller opts into, not a domain lifecycle value.
